text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Romania needs some $1.6 bilion for its crude oil imports in 1997.
- U.S. helicopter maker Bell Helicopter to resume talks with Romania on building Cobra attack helicopters in the Transylvanian city of Brasov..
- Trade unions in rail transport sector ask for a 40 percent rise of their monthly wages.
- State airline Tarom SA to mantain unchanged tariffs for international flights.
- Delta airline of the U.S. to stop flights to Romania starting April 7.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Renel RA electricity authority needs $230 million for its imports of fuel oil and gas in first quarter of 1997.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Taxes represent some 30 percent of the new price for petrol.
- Government plans cuts in wage taxes.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Corruption is a threat to the national security, President Emil Constantinescu said during a meeting of the Supreme Defence Council.
- Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea is expected to present on Wednesday a report on his 200 days in office as Bucharest mayor.
- The lower Chamber of Deputies is to call an extraordinary session on January 14.
- The government is determined to take special security measures to speed up its integration into NATO and the European Union, Defence Secretary of State Constantin Ionescu said.
ADEVARUL
- The Romanian army needs up to three billion dollars over the next six years to upgrade its equipment, Ionescu said.
- The Senate starts an extraordinary session on January 13.
- Police detained Sever Muresan, main shareholder of troubled private Dacia Felix SA bank, on charges of fraud.
- A convict in the Transylvanian city of Cluj swallowed two nails and a tin plate cut into pieces in a desperate attempt to be released.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- State television's new leadership was allegedly appointed on political criteria, former television manager Emanuel Valeriu says in full-page article.
- Ciorbea to start talks with trade unions on wage compensation after recent petrol price increases.
LIBERTATEA
- The newspaper set up a "frost hotline" for Bucharest residents who have problems with heating in their homes.
- Romanians need 140 times the average monthly wage to buy a two-room flat.
COTIDIANUL
- The defence ministry will ask for three percent of gross domestic product to be allocated for defence in 1997.
ZIUA
- Defence Secretary of State Ionescu says he is optimistic about Romania's chances of joining NATO in a first wave of expansion.
CRONICA ROMANA
- The government is determined to change Romania's economic situation even at the cost of social unrest, Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara says in interview.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- Some 2,600 Romanians have AIDS, including 2,385 children, a United Nations study shows. It says 1,192 cases are registered in the Constanta county on the Black Sea. It estimates HIV carriers in Romania at 20,000.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
